title: platform-standup-2026-03-16
content:
Attendees: Ava, Ravi, Elena, Marcus, Priya (plus ad-hoc: Josh from SRE)

Quick wins since last standup:
- Control plane migration script for service-schema v2 completed and smoke-tested on staging. No regressions in API contracts.
- Routing fallback logic improvements reduced p95 across cross-region requests by ~18% in canary (see ROUTE-391).
- Quota enforcement: hotfix applied to avoid double-counting burst requests; customer reports look stable.

Blockers / Risks:
- Auth token revocation race (PLAT-842) still intermittently failing under high churn (repro rate ~1/1000 tokens). Root cause looks like ordering between revocation write and cache invalidation. Elena is pairing with infra to instrument write ordering in Redis.
- Control plane DB migration has one remaining locked index step that needs maintenance window on prod; ops wants to schedule next Tue 02:00 UTC. Concern: peak traffic in APAC might be impacted if not throttled. Action: Marcus to propose throttling policy and coordinate with SRE.

Detailed notes by area:
- Control plane (Ava / Marcus)
  - Migration status: schema v2 rollout on canary -> staging -> limited prod. Canary results good, staging load test passed 10k req/s for 10m.
  - Next: schedule prod maintenance for index change (JIRA PLAT-842). Draft runbook in PR 1283. Need final sign-off from security for backup retention policy.
  - Action: Marcus to open downtime calendar invite and ops checklist by EOD Monday.

- Routing (Ravi)
  - Smart routing fallback: fix for primary->secondary failover latency regression landed in branch; canary shows improved p99 for cross-region failover.
  - Ongoing: add more telemetry to differentiate between network vs capacity fallback. Proposed metrics: fallback_reason, routed_region, backend_queue_depth.
  - Action: Ravi to add dashboards and a synthetic test case for region failover before next deploy.

- Auth (Elena)
  - Token revocation race: added additional CAS on cache invalidation; perf impact negligible in staging but need longer soak.
  - OAuth provider rotation: rollout plan approved; will begin next week for non-critical tenants.
  - Action: Elena will run extended soak on staging through Wednesday and report.

- Quotas & Billing (Priya)
  - Quota throttles: tuned per-tenant burst window to reduce 429s for long-tail customers; initial telemetry shows 12% drop in false-throttles.
  - Billing reconciliation: small discrepancy flagged for 2026-02-28 batch; finance and billing infra investigating. Possible root cause: rounding in usage aggregation script.
  - Action: Priya to sync with finance on Friday and file follow-up ticket if needed.

Open action items (owners & ETA):
- Marcus: Prod maintenance window + throttling policy (ETA: 2026-03-17 EOD)
- Elena: Staging soak for revocation CAS change (ETA: 2026-03-18)
- Ravi: Add routing telemetry + synthetic test (ETA: 2026-03-20)
- Priya: Billing sync with finance (ETA: 2026-03-19)
- Ava: Final review of runbook & security sign-off for migration (ETA: 2026-03-17)

Notes / questions to follow up:
- Need decision on whether to perform index change during low APAC hours or roll partial index update with online schema change tool. Ops preference leans to low-hours window.
- Confirm SLA communication for customers if maintenance is needed. Customer success to draft a short notice once maintenance slot confirmed.

Misc / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding rate-limit headers in responses to help clients self-backoff (RFC-style). Not blocking current work but useful long-term.
- Investigate possibility of moving revocation cache to a strongly-consistent store for high-churn tenants; tradeoff: higher cost and latency.

TL;DR: Migration and routing fixes progressing; token revocation race still needs soak; scheduling prod index change is highest-priority coordination item this week.

Links / refs: JIRA PLAT-842 (auth/revocation), JIRA ROUTE-391 (routing fallback), GH PR 1283 (migration runbook + scripts), Slack thread #platform-weekly for quick syncs.
